question.worked_solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{7-(2x+4)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{7(1-(2x+4)^{2}/7)}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{7}\cdot \sqrt{1-(2x+4)^{2}/7}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(2x+4)^{2}/7}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-((2x+4)/\sqrt{7})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

This resembles the basic integral for inverse sine:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡u+C
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u$ as the variable, we have $(\frac{2x+4}{\sqrt{7}}).$

So, let's perform the substitution 

$$
u=\frac{2x+4}{\sqrt{7}}.
$$

Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{7}}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we write the integral in terms of $u,$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{7-(2x+4)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-((2x+4)/\sqrt{7})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arcsin}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{2x+4}{\sqrt{7}})+C\end{aligned}
$$
